exposure: Clinical diagnosis of third-degree sphincter tears (grades 3a+b, 3c)
outcome: Agreement between clinical diagnosis and 3D-transperineal ultrasound findings regarding EAS and IAS muscle lesions
cohort: The study participants were 85 women diagnosed with third-degree obstetric anal sphincter tears who underwent a 3D-transperineal ultrasound examination 3-7 days postpartum.
finding: There was moderate agreement between clinical examination and 3D-transperineal ultrasound for diagnosing grade 3a+b and 3c perineal tears, revealing discrepancies where clinical examination missed IAS lesions in some cases and ultrasound did not confirm IAS defects in others.
